observation.visible_scene: A snowy town main street at night. Brick storefronts line the left side (a lit "BikeSparks" sign is visible), ornate lampposts wrapped in string lights stand on both sides, a red fire hydrant sits on the right sidewalk, and snow falls continuously over a wet, reflective asphalt road. Traffic occupies two directions: an oncoming lane on the left (headlights facing the camera) and a receding lane on the right (taillights). A white SUV with illuminated taillights travels away down the right side; a queue of oncoming cars with headlights advances slowly in the left lane; a dark snow-topped SUV with bright headlights approaches in the near left lane; and a dark minivan enters the foreground.
visible_changes: The near oncoming dark SUV with headlights grows larger as it approaches and then exits the frame at the left edge around the middle of the excerpt.
A dark minivan enters from the bottom-left foreground, moves across toward the centre, and proceeds away from the camera down the street, its red taillights becoming visible and staying lit.
The white SUV in the right lane steadily recedes, appearing smaller and farther down the street from first to last frame.
The line of oncoming cars (a dark sedan, then a silver/white car) creeps slowly toward the camera in the left lane.
Snowflakes drift downward across the whole scene; headlight and taillight reflections shift on the wet pavement as vehicles move.
Background elements (buildings, decorated lampposts, hydrant, signs) remain fixed in position, indicating little or no camera movement.
outside_clip_unknowns: The state of the scene before the oncoming SUV entered and after the minivan and white SUV leave the visible area.
Whether the middle-row cars are queued in traffic or parked is not fully resolvable from the slow apparent motion.
What triggers or follows any vehicle's change of speed.
uncertain_details: Exact speed and lane discipline of the oncoming queue (motion is small and partly obscured by snow and glare).
Whether any slight camera drift is present versus purely static framing.
